title: NEXT F Webhook Registry
description: Canonical outbound Webhook configuration, security, delivery, resilience and observability contracts layered on the NEXT F Event Registry.

categories.label: Foundation
categories.description: Core references, environment, ownership, event exposure and data-access boundaries.

categories.label: Endpoints
categories.description: Destination URL, verification, health, outbound network and authentication contracts.

categories.label: Subscriptions
categories.description: Event selection, filters, states, pause behavior and endpoint bindings.

categories.label: Payload & HTTP
categories.description: Webhook body, headers, response handling and canonical HTTP representation.

categories.label: Signing & Security
categories.description: HMAC signing, key references, secret rotation and replay resistance.

categories.label: Delivery
categories.description: Logical deliveries, attempts, requests, responses, failures and HTTP outcome classification.

categories.label: Retry & Resilience
categories.description: Backoff, timeouts, rate limits, queueing, dead-lettering and manual redelivery.

categories.label: Operations & Observability
categories.description: Testing, summaries, logs, retention, redaction and metrics.

schemas.name: Webhook Data Access Policy
schemas.description: Explicitly defines which event data classifications a subscription may receive.
schemas.purpose: Separates event webhook eligibility from authorization to disclose its payload.

fields.description: Whether personal data is explicitly authorized.
Whether sensitive data is explicitly authorized.
Whether financial data is explicitly authorized.

validationRules.description: Only classifications necessary for the approved integration purpose may be enabled.
webhookEligible does not itself authorize disclosure.
Secret-class data is never allowed through generic webhook payloads.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Dead Letter
schemas.description: Terminal record for a delivery that cannot be completed within permitted retry/defer policy.
schemas.purpose: Preserves bounded operational evidence and enables controlled manual diagnosis/redelivery.

validationRules.description: Dead-lettering ends automatic retry processing for the Delivery.
Dead-letter metadata is retained for 30 days by default.
Manual redelivery is permitted only inside the configured window, default 7 days after terminal outcome.
Dead-letter status does not extend exact payload retention indefinitely.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery
schemas.description: One logical outbound delivery created for one subscription and one canonical Event.
schemas.purpose: Provides stable retry/idempotency identity across all HTTP attempts.

validationRules.description: At most one logical Delivery may exist for the same `(subscriptionId,eventId)`.
Automatic retries and manual redelivery create new Attempts under the same logical Delivery.
All attempts preserve the original canonical Event ID and Event semantics.
Terminal outcome history cannot be rewritten; later redelivery is recorded as a new Attempt.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Attempt
schemas.description: One concrete HTTP attempt belonging to a logical webhook Delivery.
schemas.purpose: Preserves per-attempt timing, request outcome and retry history without changing the Event.

validationRules.description: attemptNumber increases monotonically within one logical Delivery.
Automatic attempt creation respects the active retry policy.
Stored attempt records contain only redacted/safe request and response metadata.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Failure
schemas.description: Canonical failure record for one webhook attempt or terminal delivery outcome.
schemas.purpose: Normalizes network, policy, configuration and HTTP failures for retry and diagnostics.

validationRules.description: code must exist in the webhook failure-code vocabulary.
classification and retryable must agree with canonical failure policy unless an explicitly documented policy override applies.
message/details never include secrets or unrestricted receiver content.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Log Record
schemas.description: Redacted operational log record for webhook processing.
schemas.purpose: Supports troubleshooting while keeping secret and sensitive diagnostics bounded.

validationRules.description: Secrets, signatures, authorization and sensitive URL values are redacted before storage.
Normal logs never persist arbitrary raw request/response bodies.
Diagnostic metadata must be size-bounded.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Metric Snapshot
schemas.description: Time-bounded aggregate metrics for webhook delivery health.
schemas.purpose: Supports dashboards without using raw delivery logs as analytics records.

validationRules.description: windowEnd must be later than windowStart.
All metric counts are non-negative.
Snapshot does not embed event payloads, personal data or secrets.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Queue Policy
schemas.description: Queueing and pause behavior for pending webhook deliveries.
schemas.purpose: Defines finite deferred retention and best-effort processing order.

fields.description: Maximum retention while endpoint/subscription is paused.

validationRules.description: FIFO is best effort for initial delivery; retries may overtake later deliveries.
Webhook arrival order is never authoritative; consumers use canonical Event ordering/correlation metadata.
Paused deliveries may be deferred for at most 72 hours by default.
Historical backfill is disabled in V1.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Request
schemas.description: Sanitized metadata describing the exact outbound HTTP request used for an attempt.
schemas.purpose: Supports troubleshooting without persisting secrets or unrestricted raw headers.

fields.description: Destination URL with sensitive query values redacted.
Non-secret checksum of exact serialized body bytes.

validationRules.description: Webhook delivery method is POST.
Authorization, signature, secret-backed custom headers and sensitive URL query values are removed/redacted before persistence.
Exact payload retention is governed separately and is not implied by this diagnostic record.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Response
schemas.description: Bounded sanitized response metadata for one webhook Attempt.
schemas.purpose: Supports outcome classification while preventing receiver responses from becoming business authority.

fields.description: Number of response bytes read up to policy limit.

validationRules.description: Normal response bodies cannot create authoritative NEXT F business state.
Default diagnostic body read/retention is capped at 65536 bytes.
Sensitive values must be redacted before persistence.
Only endpoint verification defines a semantic response-body challenge contract.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Delivery Summary
schemas.description: Compact safe summary of a logical webhook delivery for dashboards and lists.
schemas.purpose: Provides operational visibility without exposing retained event payloads or secrets.

validationRules.description: Summary never embeds the canonical event payload.
Summary never exposes authentication/signature material.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Endpoint
schemas.description: Verified outbound HTTPS destination used by one or more webhook subscriptions.
schemas.purpose: Defines the destination without exposing secret material.

validationRules.description: Endpoint URL must use HTTPS.
Endpoint cannot become active until challenge verification succeeds.
Delivery and verification requests must not automatically follow redirects.
Destination resolution must be revalidated at connection time against outbound-network rules.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Endpoint Authentication
schemas.description: Optional structured authentication sent in addition to mandatory NEXT F webhook signing.
schemas.purpose: Supports receiver authentication without exposing arbitrary secret-bearing headers.

validationRules.description: Destination authentication never replaces NEXT F HMAC webhook signing.
Secret value is never returned through the contract or public/browser configuration.
headerName may not override reserved protocol, proxy, cookie or hop-by-hop headers.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Endpoint Health
schemas.description: Operational health state derived from logical webhook delivery outcomes.
schemas.purpose: Provides consistent degradation, recovery and pause behavior.

validationRules.description: Default degradation occurs after 5 consecutive failed logical deliveries.
Default auto-pause occurs after 20 consecutive failed logical deliveries.
A successful logical delivery resets the consecutive failure count.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Endpoint Network Policy
schemas.description: Outbound network policy applied to endpoint verification and deliveries.
schemas.purpose: Provides SSRF-resistant destination controls.

fields.description: Whether private network destinations are allowed.
Whether DNS/IP resolution is revalidated at connection time.

validationRules.description: V1 supports public-internet destinations only.
Private, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved and cloud-metadata addresses are prohibited.
URL user-info credentials are prohibited.
Resolved addresses must be rechecked immediately before connection.
Automatic redirects are prohibited.
Default permitted ports are 443 and 8443.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Endpoint Verification
schemas.description: State and evidence for proving control of a webhook destination.
schemas.purpose: Prevents delivery to arbitrary unverified destinations.

validationRules.description: Challenges expire after the configured verification TTL.
Success requires HTTP 200 and exact challenge echo.
Verification uses the same outbound network, signing, timeout and redaction controls as normal delivery.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Endpoint Verification Payload
schemas.description: Signed payload sent to verify a webhook destination.
schemas.purpose: Provides a non-business synthetic challenge that proves receiver control.

validationRules.description: Verification payload is a protocol message, not a canonical domain Event.
challenge must be cryptographically unpredictable.
Verification request must be signed using the active webhook signing policy.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Endpoint Verification Response
schemas.description: Expected receiver response during endpoint verification.
schemas.purpose: Defines the one response flow whose body has protocol semantics.

fields.description: Exact challenge value received in the verification request.

validationRules.description: HTTP status must be exactly 200.
challenge must exactly equal the active, unexpired challenge.
Response body does not create any business state.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Environment Binding
schemas.description: Binds a webhook object to exactly one Site environment.
schemas.purpose: Prevents preview, staging and production event delivery from crossing environment boundaries.

validationRules.description: One endpoint/subscription is bound to exactly one environment.
Events from another environment must never be delivered through the binding.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Event Exposure
schemas.description: Resolved exposure decision for one canonical event and webhook subscription.
schemas.purpose: Produces an auditable allow/deny decision before a delivery is created.

fields.description: Whether the Event Registry marks the event webhook-eligible.
Whether the exact event is selected by the subscription.
Whether event and subscription environments match.
Whether the subscription data policy authorizes the payload.
Canonical denial reason when not allowed.

validationRules.description: allowed may be true only when eligible, selected, environmentMatches and dataAuthorized are all true.
Wildcard event selection is not permitted in V1.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Event Selection
schemas.description: Exact canonical Event allow-list for a webhook subscription.
schemas.purpose: Prevents ambiguous wildcard subscriptions and provides deterministic delivery eligibility.

fields.description: Contract Registry version used to validate selection.

relationships.description: Each selected key must resolve to a canonical Event definition.

validationRules.description: At least one exact event key is required for an active subscription.
Wildcard and prefix matching are prohibited in V1.
Selected definitions must have webhookEligible=true.
Duplicate event keys are prohibited.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Failure Classification
schemas.description: Controlled classification vocabulary used to decide terminal, deferred, retry or endpoint-disable behavior.
schemas.purpose: Separates stable operational handling from provider-specific exception strings.

fields.description: Whether an automatic retry may be scheduled.
Whether the current Attempt is terminal.

validationRules.description: Classification values are controlled by the registry.
An Attempt can be terminal while the logical Delivery remains retry-scheduled.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Header Policy
schemas.description: Required and reserved HTTP header contract for webhook requests.
schemas.purpose: Ensures receivers can authenticate, identify and diagnose deliveries consistently.

fields.description: Whether controlled custom headers are supported.

validationRules.description: All protocol headers defined in registry/webhooks/headers.json must be sent.
Custom configuration cannot override reserved headers.
NextF-Webhook-Signature is always redacted in diagnostics.
Hop-by-hop/proxy/cookie headers cannot be customer-defined.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook HTTP Outcome Policy
schemas.description: Canonical mapping from receiver HTTP status classes to webhook delivery behavior.
schemas.purpose: Prevents customer projects from inventing incompatible HTTP retry semantics.

validationRules.description: 200-299 is success.
408, 425, 429 and 5xx are retryable within retry budget.
3xx is terminal and never auto-followed.
410 is terminal and disables the endpoint.
Other 4xx statuses are terminal.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Pause Policy
schemas.description: Defines how deliveries behave while a subscription or endpoint is paused.
schemas.purpose: Prevents indefinite unbounded retention while allowing short operational recovery.

fields.description: Whether eligible deliveries are deferred while paused.

validationRules.description: Default maximum paused queue retention is 72 hours.
Deferred deliveries exceeding the window become dead-lettered.
Indefinite queue retention is prohibited.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Payload Envelope
schemas.description: Canonical outbound JSON envelope wrapping an exact NEXT F domain Event occurrence.
schemas.purpose: Adds delivery metadata without changing the authoritative Event identity or payload semantics.

validationRules.description: Canonical Event identity, key, version and semantics must not be rewritten for the receiver.
All retries/redeliveries of one logical Delivery preserve the same canonical eventId.
Payload is serialized as UTF-8 JSON.
Serialized payload must not exceed the configured maximum, default 256 KiB.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Payload Policy
schemas.description: Canonical serialization, size and enrichment rules for outbound webhook bodies.
schemas.purpose: Prevents uncontrolled data enrichment, compression ambiguity and oversized deliveries.

fields.description: Whether arbitrary current entity snapshots can be appended.

validationRules.description: Default is application/json; charset=utf-8, UTF-8, identity encoding and 262144 bytes.
Unrestricted entity snapshot enrichment is prohibited.
Signature is calculated over the exact serialized raw body bytes sent on the wire.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Rate Policy
schemas.description: Per-endpoint delivery rate and concurrency controls.
schemas.purpose: Protects both NEXT F delivery infrastructure and receiver endpoints from unbounded bursts.

fields.description: Maximum request start rate per endpoint.

validationRules.description: Default is 10 requests per second and 4 concurrent requests per endpoint.
Retries, redeliveries, tests and verification requests are subject to applicable network/rate controls.
Rate limiting must not be interpreted as strict cross-delivery ordering.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Redaction Policy
schemas.description: Mandatory diagnostic redaction rules.
schemas.purpose: Prevents secret and sensitive transport values from leaking through logs, UI or persisted diagnostics.

fields.description: Always redact NEXT F webhook signatures.
Always redact secret-backed custom header values.
Redact sensitive URL query parameter values.

validationRules.description: Redaction happens before diagnostic persistence.
Mandatory secret/auth/signature redactions cannot be disabled.
Redaction is not a substitute for data-access/exposure policy.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Redelivery Request
schemas.description: Audited operator request to attempt delivery again for an existing logical Delivery.
schemas.purpose: Supports controlled recovery without creating a duplicate canonical Event or duplicate logical Delivery.

validationRules.description: Accepted redelivery creates another Attempt on the same logical Delivery.
Redelivery never creates or mutates the canonical Event.
Request must be inside the exact-payload/manual-redelivery availability window.
Manual redelivery requires explicit administrative permission and audit.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Replay Protection
schemas.description: Receiver-side replay-resistance expectations for signed webhook requests.
schemas.purpose: Combines request timestamp validation with stable Event and Delivery identifiers.

validationRules.description: Reject otherwise valid signatures outside the configured freshness window unless implementing a documented redelivery exception based on the new request timestamp.
Receivers should record processed eventId/delivery identity for their own idempotency needs.
Each retry has a fresh signature timestamp while retaining the same canonical eventId and logical deliveryId.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Request Header
schemas.description: Controlled non-reserved request header configured for a webhook endpoint.
schemas.purpose: Allows bounded receiver-specific metadata without creating an arbitrary raw-request interface.

fields.description: Whether diagnostics must always redact the value.

validationRules.description: Use either literal value or secretReference, never both.
Reserved NEXT F, Authorization, proxy, cookie and hop-by-hop headers cannot be overridden.
Header name must satisfy HTTP token syntax.
Header values cannot contain CR/LF or control-character injection.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Response Policy
schemas.description: Defines how receiver HTTP responses are interpreted.
schemas.purpose: Treats status as delivery outcome and response body as bounded diagnostics except during endpoint verification.

fields.description: Maximum response bytes retained/read for diagnostics.
Whether normal response bodies can create NEXT F business state.

validationRules.description: HTTP 200 through 299 are successful deliveries.
3xx responses are terminal and never followed automatically.
408, 425, 429 and 5xx responses are retryable subject to policy.
Other 4xx responses are terminal except 410 additionally disables the endpoint.
Normal delivery response bodies are diagnostic only.
At most 65536 response bytes are read/retained for diagnostics by default.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Retention Policy
schemas.description: Retention windows for payloads, diagnostics and delivery metadata.
schemas.purpose: Balances redelivery/debugging needs with data minimization.

fields.description: Exact retry/redelivery payload retention after terminal state.

validationRules.description: Defaults are 7d exact payload, 24h response snippet, 30d delivery metadata, 30d dead-letter metadata and 7d manual redelivery.
Future privacy/data-retention policy may reduce these windows.
Sensitive exact payload retention is never indefinite.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Retry Policy
schemas.description: Bounded automatic retry schedule for retryable webhook failures.
schemas.purpose: Defines deterministic retry limits while allowing bounded jitter and Retry-After handling.

fields.description: Maximum total attempts including initial attempt.
Maximum percentage jitter around base delay.
Whether bounded Retry-After can influence scheduling.

validationRules.description: Default maximum is 8 total attempts including initial.
Default delays are 60, 300, 900, 3600, 14400, 43200 and 86400 seconds.
Default jitter is 20 percent.
Accepted Retry-After is bounded between 5 and 86400 seconds.
Retries must terminate and transition to a terminal/dead-letter state.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Secret Rotation
schemas.description: Finite-overlap rotation record for webhook signing secrets.
schemas.purpose: Allows receivers to migrate from an old signing secret without an unbounded multi-key verification period.

validationRules.description: Default overlap window is 24 hours.
During overlap, delivery may include verifiable signatures for both active keys using documented v1 entries.
An overlap must always have an explicit end time.
Old key is no longer accepted after rotation completion.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Signature Policy
schemas.description: Mandatory HMAC signature protocol for every NEXT F webhook request.
schemas.purpose: Allows receivers to verify request authenticity and body integrity without exposing the signing secret.

validationRules.description: V1 uses HMAC-SHA256.
V1 signs `<unix-seconds>.<exact raw UTF-8 request body bytes>`.
Signature header format is `t=<unix-seconds>,v1=<lowercase-hex-hmac>`.
Receivers should compare computed signatures using constant-time comparison.
Receiver must validate timestamp freshness; default tolerance is 300 seconds.
Signature validation is independent of optional destination authentication.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Signing Key Reference
schemas.description: Write-only server-side reference to a webhook HMAC signing secret.
schemas.purpose: Separates secret material from browser-visible endpoint and subscription configuration.

fields.description: When key becomes valid for signing.

validationRules.description: New signing secrets require at least 32 bytes of cryptographic entropy.
Raw signing secret is shown only through an explicit one-time secure setup flow and is not readable afterward.
Secret material never appears in browser bundles, registry data or normal API responses.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Subscription
schemas.description: Explicit binding between one verified endpoint and an exact allow-list of canonical Events.
schemas.purpose: Controls which eligible domain facts may create outbound webhook deliveries.

validationRules.description: Subscription can become active only when endpoint is active and verified.
V1 subscriptions select exact canonical event keys; wildcards are prohibited.
All selected events must be webhookEligible in the Event Registry.
Subscription and endpoint environment must match.
V1 does not backfill historical events before activation.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Subscription Filter
schemas.description: Optional bounded filter applied after event selection and before delivery creation.
schemas.purpose: Allows narrow subscription routing without introducing arbitrary executable predicates.

validationRules.description: Filter paths must be explicitly permitted by the selected Event definition or platform policy.
Regular-expression execution, scripts and arbitrary expressions are prohibited in V1.
Matching a field does not grant permission to expose that field in the outbound payload.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Subscription Ownership
schemas.description: Records the Organization/Site ownership boundary for a webhook subscription.
schemas.purpose: Enforces tenant isolation for webhook configuration and delivery operations.

validationRules.description: siteId must belong to organizationId.
Caller supplied IDs are never sufficient authorization.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Subscription State
schemas.description: Lifecycle state for a webhook subscription.
schemas.purpose: Separates human/configuration state from individual delivery state.

validationRules.description: Active requires verified endpoint, valid selection and valid data policy.
Disabled subscriptions do not resume automatically.
Manual state transitions must be auditable.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Test Delivery
schemas.description: Synthetic signed delivery used to test an endpoint and receiver implementation.
schemas.purpose: Allows safe diagnostics without impersonating a real domain Event or mutating business state.

validationRules.description: Test payload cannot use a real canonical Event ID or claim a real business event occurred.
Test delivery cannot create authoritative customer/business state.
Network, signature, timeout, rate and redaction controls apply to tests.
Test requests are auditable.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Timeout Policy
schemas.description: Outbound connection and total execution timeout contract.
schemas.purpose: Caps resource usage and prevents slow receivers from holding delivery workers indefinitely.

validationRules.description: Defaults are 5 seconds connect and 15 seconds total.
Total timeout must be greater than or equal to connect timeout.
Deployments may tighten values but cannot remove finite timeouts.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.

schemas.name: Webhook Reference
schemas.description: Compact reference to a webhook endpoint, subscription, delivery or attempt.
schemas.purpose: Allows schemas and logs to reference webhook objects without embedding full sensitive records.

validationRules.description: Reference IDs are opaque and must not encode secrets or personal data.
kind must match the referenced object type.

notes: Webhook registry contracts are configuration/operations data and are never public website content.
Authorization is configured through structured destination authentication, not arbitrary custom headers.
Header values classified as secrets are never displayed after initial secure setup.

failureCodes.description: DNS resolution failed or returned no allowed address.
Resolved destination is private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast or otherwise prohibited.
Connection was not established before the configured connect timeout.
TLS negotiation or certificate validation failed; repeated configuration failures may degrade endpoint health.
Connection closed unexpectedly.
Total request execution exceeded the configured timeout.
Serialized webhook payload exceeded the permitted maximum.
A 3xx response was returned. Redirects are never automatically followed.
Receiver returned HTTP 401.
Receiver returned HTTP 403.
Receiver returned HTTP 404.
Receiver returned HTTP 410 and explicitly indicates the endpoint is gone.
Receiver returned HTTP 408.
Receiver returned HTTP 425.
Receiver returned HTTP 429. A valid bounded Retry-After may influence scheduling.
Receiver returned a non-retryable 4xx response.
Receiver returned a retryable 5xx response.
Response body exceeded the diagnostic read limit.
Delivery cannot start because destination verification is incomplete.
Delivery cannot start because the endpoint is disabled.
Delivery is held while the subscription is paused.
Delivery cannot start because the subscription is disabled.
Selected canonical Event is not webhook eligible.
Event and subscription environment bindings do not match.
Subscription is not approved for the Event data classification.
Event is not explicitly selected by the subscription.
Webhook configuration failed contract validation.
Retryable failures exhausted the permitted attempt budget.
A deferred delivery exceeded the paused-subscription retention window.
Delivery was explicitly cancelled by an authorized platform operation.
An unexpected transport failure occurred; bounded retry policy still applies.

events.name: Inventory Low
events.description: Available quantity crosses from above to at/below the configured low-stock threshold.

events.name: Inventory Out of Stock
events.description: Available quantity crosses to the configured out-of-stock condition.

events.name: Inventory Released
events.description: A prior inventory reservation is released.

events.name: Inventory Reserved
events.description: Available inventory is atomically reserved for an eligible workflow.

events.name: Inventory Transferred
events.description: An inventory transfer between canonical locations is committed without creating/destroying quantity.

events.name: Lead Assigned
events.description: Lead assignment changes to a canonical actor.

events.name: Lead Created
events.description: A canonical Lead record is committed from an accepted source or authorized manual creation.

events.name: Lead Merged
events.description: Two or more duplicate Lead records are explicitly merged according to policy.

events.name: Lead Status Changed
events.description: Lead status changes from one canonical Site status to another.

events.name: Lead Updated
events.description: Material Lead business data is committed.

events.name: Media Created
events.description: A media asset record is committed.

events.name: Media Deleted
events.description: A media asset record is deleted/retired according to policy.

events.name: Media Updated
events.description: Media metadata is materially updated.

events.name: Navigation Updated
events.description: Navigation structure is materially changed.

events.name: Order Archived
events.description: Order becomes archived without destroying transaction history.

events.name: Order Cancelled
events.description: Order cancellation is committed after all guards pass.

events.name: Order Completed
events.description: Order completion guards pass and operational status becomes completed.

events.name: Order Created
events.description: A canonical Order is committed from a completed Checkout or authorized order-creation workflow.

events.name: Order Fulfilled
events.description: Fulfillment reconciliation confirms all required fulfillable quantity is fulfilled.

events.name: Order On Hold
events.description: Order operational status enters on-hold.

events.name: Order Paid
events.description: Payment reconciliation determines the Order payable balance is fully satisfied.

events.name: Order Partially Fulfilled
events.description: Fulfillment reconciliation confirms some but not all fulfillable quantity is fulfilled.

events.name: Order Partially Paid
events.description: Payment reconciliation determines the Order has received a positive amount below the payable total.

events.name: Order Partially Refunded
events.description: Successful refunds reduce captured funds while a positive net captured amount remains.

events.name: Order Refunded
events.description: Successful refunds fully reconcile the refundable captured amount according to the Order state.

events.name: Order Updated
events.description: Allowed non-historical Order metadata changes are committed.

events.name: Payment Authorized
events.description: A payment provider authorization has been validated and reconciled to a canonical authorization.

events.name: Payment Captured
events.description: A validated capture succeeds and is recorded canonically.

events.name: Payment Created
events.description: A canonical Payment record is created for an Order.

events.name: Payment Failed
events.description: A Payment attempt or Payment reaches authoritative failure state.

events.name: Payment Succeeded
events.description: A Payment reaches successful settled/captured state according to its provider-neutral contract.

events.name: Product Archived
events.description: A Product enters archived state.

events.name: Product Created
events.description: A Product is created.

events.name: Product Published
events.description: A Product becomes eligible for active storefront publication.

events.name: Product Updated
events.description: A Product is materially updated.

events.name: Redirect Created
events.description: A canonical redirect is created.

events.name: Redirect Deleted
events.description: A canonical redirect is removed.

events.name: Redirect Updated
events.description: A canonical redirect is materially updated.

events.name: Refund Created
events.description: A canonical Refund request/record is created.

events.name: Refund Failed
events.description: A refund attempt reaches authoritative failure state without applying successful financial effect.

events.name: Refund Succeeded
events.description: A refund succeeds with the provider and is reconciled canonically.

events.name: Return Approved
events.description: A Return request is approved.

events.name: Return Cancelled
events.description: A Return request is cancelled before completion.

events.name: Return Completed
events.description: Return resolution is completed.

events.name: Return Received
events.description: Returned goods/services are recorded as received where applicable.

events.name: Return Rejected
events.description: A Return request is rejected without refund/restock side effects.

events.name: Return Requested
events.description: A customer or authorized operator creates a Return request.

events.name: Product Review Approved
events.description: A Product Review passes moderation and becomes approved.

events.name: Product Review Created
events.description: A Product Review is submitted and stored for moderation.

events.name: Product Review Published
events.description: An approved Product Review becomes publicly eligible.

events.name: Product Review Rejected
events.description: A Product Review is rejected by moderation.

events.name: SEO Updated
events.description: Canonical SEO metadata/configuration is materially updated.

events.name: Shipment Created
events.description: A Shipment record is created for a Fulfillment.

events.name: Shipment Delivered
events.description: Delivery evidence is reconciled and the Shipment reaches delivered state.

events.name: Shipment Delivery Failed
events.description: A delivery attempt reaches a provider-neutral failed-delivery state.

events.name: Shipment Dispatched
events.description: A Shipment is handed to the carrier/dispatch workflow with required evidence.

events.name: Sitemap Updated
events.description: A Site sitemap configuration or generated publication set materially changes.

events.name: Product Variant Created
events.description: A Product Variant is created.

events.name: Product Variant Updated
events.description: A Product Variant is materially updated.
